tasks.title: ngv2/llm_client.py — injected LLM client seam for PoC synthesis (io_adapter, smoke-gated)
acceptance_criteria: `ngv2/llm_client.py` is created as a NEW single-file, whole-file module exactly matching the validated artifact in the brief.
`.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_llm_client_wired.py -q` passes GREEN (no `cd` prefix; runs in the staging worktree).
Module is importable with only stdlib + typing at module scope; the `anthropic` SDK is imported lazily INSIDE `make_anthropic_client` and never on the import path or any oracle path.
The request contract (`messages`/`model`/`max_tokens`/`system`) is passed through unchanged to the injected `complete` callable.
`complete_messages` supports multi-turn message lists; `complete_text` wraps a single user prompt.
`LLMError` is raised when no `complete` seam is injected and on non-transient completion failures.
On a rate-limit error the client calls `cascade.report_rate_limit(model, error_text=...)` and retries with the next `cascade.get_active_model()`, up to `max_retries`.
`make_anthropic_client` is a callable factory returning a `CompleteFn`; it is never invoked by the oracle.
`ngv2/model_cascade.py` is NOT modified; the cascade is consumed only via the injected object.

spec.objective: Create the new whole-file module `ngv2/llm_client.py` as an injected LLM client seam (io_adapter, smoke-gated) for PoC synthesis, proven GREEN against the already-committed oracle `tests/test_llm_client_wired.py`. The model edge is an injected `complete` callable so the oracle is hermetic; the real network path lives behind `make_anthropic_client` with a lazy `anthropic` import.
functional_requirements: Define module-level `DEFAULT_MODEL = 'claude-fable-5'`, `DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 4096`, `CompleteFn = Callable[..., str]`, and `RATE_LIMIT_MARKERS`, importing only stdlib `typing` at module scope.
Define `class LLMError(RuntimeError)` raised on non-transient completion failure or when no completion seam is injected.

`LLMClient.__init__(complete=None, *, model=None, cascade=None, max_retries=3)` stores the injected seam, defaults `self.model` to `DEFAULT_MODEL`, holds the optional cascade-shaped object, and initializes `last_request`/`last_response` to None.
`_active_model()` returns `cascade.get_active_model()` (falling back to `self.model`) when a cascade is present, else `self.model`, swallowing cascade exceptions.
`complete_text(prompt, *, system=None, max_tokens=DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS)` wraps the prompt into a single `{'role':'user','content':prompt}` message and delegates to `complete_messages`.

`complete_messages(messages, *, system=None, max_tokens=DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS)` raises `LLMError` when no seam is injected, otherwise passes `messages`/`model`/`max_tokens`/`system` through to the injected `complete`, records `last_request`/`last_response`, and returns the assistant text.

On an exception whose text looks rate-limited (per `RATE_LIMIT_MARKERS` via `_looks_rate_limited`) and while `attempts < max_retries`, call `cascade.report_rate_limit(model, error_text=...)` (when a cascade is present) and retry with the next active model; non-transient errors are wrapped and re-raised as `LLMError`.

`make_anthropic_client(*, api_key=None, model=None)` lazily imports `anthropic` inside the body, constructs the SDK client, and returns a `CompleteFn` that calls `client.messages.create` and concatenates the response `content` text blocks.
spec.interfaces: ngv2/llm_client.py exposes `LLMClient`, `LLMError`, `DEFAULT_MODEL` (=='claude-fable-5'), `CompleteFn`, and `make_anthropic_client(*, api_key=None, model=None)`. The injected seam signature is `complete(messages, *, model, max_tokens, system) -> str`. `LLMClient` exposes `complete_text(prompt, *, system=None, max_tokens=DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS)` and `complete_messages(messages, *, system=None, max_tokens=DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS)`, plus public attributes `model`, `last_request`, `last_response`.
edge_cases: No `complete` seam injected (`complete=None`): both `complete_text` and `complete_messages` raise `LLMError`.
Rate-limit error with no cascade: retries with `self.model` until `max_retries` is exhausted, then raises `LLMError`.
Rate-limit error with a cascade: `report_rate_limit(model, error_text=...)` is invoked and `get_active_model()` advances the model on retry.
Cascade methods themselves raise: exceptions from `get_active_model()`/`report_rate_limit()` are swallowed and fall back to `self.model`.
`anthropic` not installed: module still imports because the import is lazy inside `make_anthropic_client`.
Empty/None error text passed to `_looks_rate_limited` returns False (treated as non-transient).
non_goals: No real network call in the import path or any oracle path; `anthropic` is imported lazily inside `make_anthropic_client` only.
No third-party imports at module scope (stdlib typing + the lazy anthropic only).
No tests authored — the oracle `tests/test_llm_client_wired.py` is already committed.
Do NOT modify `ngv2/model_cascade.py`; compose only with an injected cascade-shaped object.
No PoC-writing logic here (that is P4.2).

# COMMITTED ORACLE CONTRACT (authoritative; you cannot read these files at synthesis time so they are reproduced verbatim -- your code MUST make them pass):

## tests/test_llm_client_wired.py
```python
"""Oracle for P4.1 -- ngv2.llm_client injected LLM client seam.

Hermetic: the model edge is an injected canned ``complete`` callable; no network.
Asserts: default model is the latest Claude (claude-fable-5); the request/response
contract passes through (messages/model/max_tokens/system); cascade fallback fires
on a rate-limit error; a non-injected client raises; a non-transient failure maps
to LLMError. RED until ngv2/llm_client.py exists.
"""
import pytest

from ngv2.llm_client import (
    LLMClient,
    LLMError,
    DEFAULT_MODEL,
    make_anthropic_client,
)


def test_default_model_is_latest_claude():
    assert DEFAULT_MODEL == "claude-fable-5"
    assert LLMClient(lambda *a, **k: "x").model == "claude-fable-5"


def test_request_contract_passes_through():
    seen = {}

    def canned(messages, *, model, max_tokens, system):
        seen["messages"] = messages
        seen["model"] = model
        seen["max_tokens"] = max_tokens
        seen["system"] = system
        return "RESPONSE"

    client = LLMClient(canned, model="claude-fable-5")
    out = client.complete_text("hello", system="be terse", max_tokens=128)
    assert out == "RESPONSE"
    assert seen["messages"] == [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}]
    assert seen["model"] == "claude-fable-5"
    assert seen["max_tokens"] == 128
    assert seen["system"] == "be terse"
    # request/response retained for contract assertions
    assert client.last_request["model"] == "claude-fable-5"
    assert client.last_response == "RESPONSE"


def test_multiturn_messages():
    def echo(messages, *, model, max_tokens, system):
        return messages[-1]["content"].upper()

    client = LLMClient(echo)
    out = client.complete_messages(
        [{"role": "user", "content": "a"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "b"},
         {"role": "user", "content": "c"}]
    )
    assert out == "C"


def test_no_seam_raises():
    with pytest.raises(LLMError):
        LLMClient(None).complete_text("x")


def test_non_transient_failure_maps_to_llmerror():
    def boom(messages, *, model, max_tokens, system):
        raise ValueError("bad request: malformed")

    with pytest.raises(LLMError):
        LLMClient(boom).complete_text("x")


def test_cascade_fallback_on_rate_limit():
    # A fake cascade: first model 'A' is rate-limited once, then 'B' succeeds.
    class FakeCascade:
        def __init__(self):
            self.order = ["model-A", "model-B"]
            self.reports = []

        def get_active_model(self):
            return self.order[0]

        def report_rate_limit(self, model, error_text=None):
            self.reports.append((model, error_text))
            self.order.pop(0)  # advance to the next model

    cascade = FakeCascade()
    calls = {"n": 0}

    def flaky(messages, *, model, max_tokens, system):
        calls["n"] += 1
        if model == "model-A":
            raise RuntimeError("429 too many requests")
        return "OK from " + model

    client = LLMClient(flaky, cascade=cascade)
    out = client.complete_text("x")
    assert out == "OK from model-B"
    assert calls["n"] == 2
    assert cascade.reports and cascade.reports[0][0] == "model-A"


def test_make_anthropic_client_is_lazy():
    # Building the real seam is a factory; it must be importable + callable as a
    # symbol even when the SDK is absent (it only imports anthropic when invoked).
    assert callable(make_anthropic_client)

```

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Canned in-memory `complete` callables: one that echoes/records its kwargs to assert the request contract, one that raises a rate-limit-marked exception, one that raises a non-transient exception. A fake cascade-shaped object with sequenced `get_active_model()` return values and a recording `report_rate_limit(model, error_text=...)`. No network access; the `anthropic` SDK is never imported by oracle paths.
